findings.fact: The player is one engine-created entity whose inherited save chain contains 277 fields and whose carried inventory remains a graph of moveable entities.
findings.evidence: The save entity table contains exactly one FENTTABLE_PLAYER and the class records total 277; carried items have owner and player-handle relationships rather than becoming class-name rows on the player.
findings.consequence: Player persistence and inventory persistence must be joined by entity identity and transition policy rather than implemented as unrelated value bags.

findings.fact: The player update is command-timed and precedes the ordinary entity think and event-queue pass.
findings.evidence: ProcessUsercmds synchronously reaches PlayerRunCommand and PlayerMove RunCommand orders PreThink player Think movement impacts and PostThink before server GameFrame.
findings.consequence: The complete player transaction must classify work per user command including replayed commands rather than assume one update per rendered frame.

findings.fact: The 157-record CBasePlayer datamap exposes ten external inputs rather than an unidentified eleventh input.
findings.evidence: Builder 0x1015af10 assigns record array 0x10580f24 and count 0x9d. Reconstruction finds ten externally named records with input flag 0x8; the superficially similar eleventh callback record is unnamed CBasePlayerPlayerDeathThink with flag 0x20 and callback 0x101668b0.
findings.consequence: The runtime input surface is complete at ten names; PlayerDeathThink belongs to lifecycle recovery rather than AcceptInput dispatch.

findings.fact: CHL2_Player PreThink has a distinct vehicle path and a live unlocked path; death processing truncates only the late live path.
findings.evidence: 0x10350830 checks saved m_bInVehicle at +0x20f4 first. That path performs client-data synchronization, time-based damage and the post-damage hook, then returns. The live path runs VtMB rules, item pre-frame, water state, retained suit power, client data and time-based damage before testing life state; PlayerDeathThink then returns before train, jump, duck, fall, stealth and final hooks.
findings.consequence: A faithful player update cannot be represented as one unconditional per-frame list, and death must not suppress the earlier damage and synchronization work.

findings.fact: The inherited CHL2 suit-power branch is still called but is Source mechanism baggage rather than an evidenced VtMB-authored rule.
findings.evidence: Vtable slot 472 resolves to 0x103528d0. Its body charges or drains +0x2464 from active-device bits +0x252c and load +0x2530, matching the inherited suit-power transaction; none of those names appears in the player datamap or established VtMB content contract.
findings.consequence: The remaster must not reproduce auxiliary suit power merely because the retail executable still executes its dormant bookkeeping; an authored VtMB consumer would be required.

findings.fact: CBasePlayer PostThink separates a live main body from a common tail, with one transformation branch that returns before the tail.
findings.evidence: 0x1016be10 skips the main body for game-over, player-locked, dead state or the slot-406 byte at +0x19f6, then reaches SimulatePlayerSimulatedEntities and the VtMB tail. The live body orders bounds and use handling, ItemPostFrame, landing, action classification and SetAnimation, sequence/frame/weapon/sound/physics updates. The Animalism beast-model transition returns directly after resetting and rerouting state.
findings.consequence: Post-move gameplay, presentation and ownership cleanup need explicit gates; treating PostThink as animation-only would omit weapon, hunger, simulated-entity and cinematic-state work.

findings.fact: Player allocation, client admission and spawn are distinct ordered stages.
findings.evidence: The registered player factory at 0x1034f270 makes classname player constructible. PutClientInServer 0x10352d70 requests that classname; factory 0x1034f1e0 allocates 0x2548 bytes and calls constructor 0x1034f330, which enters CBasePlayer construction, constructs local data at +0x2464 and installs the CHL2 vtable. Client/name binding then precedes the slot-103 Spawn dispatch.
findings.consequence: The durable player record, client connection and embodied playable reset must not be collapsed into one constructor or pawn-spawn callback.

findings.fact: Spawn establishes playable defaults under a gate shared with restore, while restore rebases durable state and placement rather than creating a second player.
findings.evidence: CBasePlayer Spawn 0x1016d260 raises +0x1e00, resets health, life, gait, movement, handles and deadlines, creates unarmed equipment, establishes collision and team membership, lowers the gate and calls OnPlacedInMap. Restore 0x1016ebd0 raises the same gate, calls inherited restore, rebases three saved times, rejoins team and placement/hull/global-player state, restores the quest registry and finalizes the restore context.
findings.consequence: New-player defaults and restored-player authority need separate transactions with the shared gate suppressing post-spawn publication during restore.

findings.fact: The command-scoped player Think step is only a due-think scheduler, and death is a staged scheduled state machine with a conditional Spawn exit.
findings.evidence: RunPlayerThink 0x101871f0 checks next-think against the command window, publishes the due curtime, clears the schedule and dispatches the registered callback. PlayerDeathThink 0x101668b0 reschedules itself, advances dying/dead gates and reaches 0x10352ed0; that helper dispatches slot 103 only under two global state bytes and never deletes the entity.
findings.consequence: No second unconditional player rules tick is required; death scheduling, input gates and conditional respawn must remain explicit.

findings.fact: Player destruction frees owned helper storage and containers but not the world entities referenced by player handles.
findings.evidence: The full destructor reached from 0x1034f4b0 and 0x1015ded0 destroys/frees the helper at +0x1d24, the helper at +0x245c and multiple dynamic containers before the inherited destructor. It contains no 224-slot inventory deletion walk and no camera-target deletion path.
findings.consequence: World/entity retirement and player-object destruction are separate ownership operations; inventory and camera handles must not imply destructor ownership.

findings.fact: Criminal, supernatural and investigate activity levels are three independent player channels with different mutation and expiry contracts.
findings.evidence: The three datamap inputs accept only integer variants and clamp to 0 through 5. Criminal and supernatural non-zero writes raise but never lower their retained level, refresh a duration derived from max(previous retained level, pl_min_act_timer), and increment separate incident counts; zero clears. Investigate writes its level directly. Supernatural expiry advances in PlayerRuleUpdate, while criminal expiry is checked by the SetAnimation law helper.
findings.consequence: A map activity volume must not treat duration -1 as indefinite or collapse investigate into the timed criminal and supernatural channels.

findings.fact: A witnessed supernatural incident is the recovered native downstream join to a rate-limited Masquerade violation; a criminal incident does not mutate Masquerade.
findings.evidence: 0x1017f4a0 calls ChangeMasqueradeLevel(+1) only after m_flMasqueradeTimerNext has elapsed and then schedules debug_masquerade_timer. 0x1017f2a0 enters only police response. ChangeMasqueradeLevel fires level and generic outputs and loads sp_masquerade_1 when the resulting value exceeds four.
findings.consequence: The faithful system needs separate activity production, NPC witness admission, Masquerade throttling and police response; an overt cast raises activity but never mutates Masquerade directly.

findings.fact: Player law admission is an activity-counter to per-NPC condition and schedule transaction, not a central zone-aware violation callback.
findings.evidence: Targeted Discipline commit 0x101e2f50 maps SupernaturalLvl to player supernatural activity and Overt to criminal activity 3. NPC update 0x1028efc0 deduplicates the two player counts, applies authored flee/attack thresholds and retains offender/origin before schedule bodies submit the incident. World-law records additionally require view cone, inspection distance and an unobstructed trace in 0x1028ebc0.
findings.consequence: The player owns severity and act identity; each NPC owns witness qualification and reaction, while Elysium verb blocking and HUD zone presentation remain upstream systems.

findings.fact: Police response is a retained highest-severity delayed transaction followed by separate pursuit and alert modes.
findings.evidence: 0x1017ed00 admits only while no hunters pursue, queues a witness handle, position and severity on a randomized debug_response_timer_min/max deadline, and replaces only a higher queued severity without moving the deadline. The due update requires the witness handle to remain valid. The deadline computes max(1, level-1) cops, applies debug_cop_grace_time suppression/delta logic, then either invokes the global NPC maker or records wait-area state. Cop pursuit counts fire start/end edges; the final cop leaving starts heightened alert, whose expiry fires OnEndCopAlertMode.
findings.consequence: Police spawning, pursuit membership and post-pursuit alert cannot be represented as one criminal-level boolean or an immediate spawn on every offense.
